one_line: Paramara king of Malwa and scholar-king of Dhara’s Sanskrit learning circle, c. 1010–1055 CE.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s to early 40s, lean but strong build, average height with a scholar-warrior bearing.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, medium brown Malwa complexion, neatly trimmed moustache and short beard along the jawline, sharp thoughtful eyes with slightly arched brows; default expression is calm, observant and gently encouraging, as if listening to a student’s recitation.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered into a high, neat topknot at the back of the crown, with the rest smoothed back; a slender gold circlet with a small central leaf-shaped ornament rests low on the forehead, and a narrow saffron cloth band is tied under the knot so its short tails fall behind.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate Paramara royal-scholarly attire: a long-sleeved, knee-length cotton angarakha in deep maroon with wrap-over front and a subtle woven diamond pattern, tied at the right side with narrow cords; over this, a soft cream-colored silk uttariya (shawl) with thin red and black borders draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back; lower garment is a neatly pleated off-white cotton dhoti wrapped to mid-calf with a broad maroon border matching the angarakha; feet in simple brown leather sandals with toe loops; jewellery limited to a single narrow gold armlet on the right arm engraved with simple floral motifs, a pair of small round gold earrings close to the ear, and a thin tulsi-bead mala around the neck; no armor, emphasizing his role as scholar-king in the learning hall rather than battlefield.
appearance.signature: A palm-leaf manuscript bundle of the Sarasvati-Kanthabharana, tied with a red cotton cord and held in his left hand, with a smooth wooden stylus tucked under the cord, symbolizing his role as grammarian among the scholars of Dhara.

ref_desc: Bhoja of Dhara is a mid-40s Malwa scholar-king with an oval medium-brown face, neat moustache and beard, black hair in a topknot with gold circlet, wearing a deep maroon angarakha, cream uttariya, off-white dhoti, simple gold jewellery, and holding a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character turnaround of Bhoja of Dhara as a dignified 11th-century Paramara scholar-king: a mid-40s Malwa man with an oval medium-brown face, sharp thoughtful eyes, neat moustache and short beard, and thick black hair gathered into a high topknot. A slender gold circlet with a small central leaf ornament rests on his forehead, with a narrow saffron cloth band tied beneath the knot so its short tails fall down his back. He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length deep maroon cotton angarakha with a wrap-over front and subtle woven diamond pattern, tied at the right side, over which a cream-colored silk uttariya with thin red and black borders is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back. His lower garment is a neatly pleated off-white cotton dhoti with a broad maroon border reaching mid-calf, and he wears simple brown leather sandals with toe loops. Jewellery is modest: a thin tulsi-bead mala, small round gold earrings, and a single narrow gold armlet engraved with floral motifs on his right arm. In his left hand he carries a tied bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts of Sarasvati-Kanthabharana with a visible red cotton cord and a smooth wooden stylus tucked under it, while his right hand is relaxed as if gesturing to students. Use a palette dominated by deep maroon, cream, off-white, gold, and brown, and present him in a calm, observant pose suitable for a royal-scholarly setting in Dhara’s learning halls.
